in_sanskrit.name: अङ्ग
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The root word 'ang' in Sanskrit refers to a limb, part, or member. It is also used metaphorically to denote a group, division, or even a quality or attribute. In Hindu mythology, the 'Anga' Maruts are a group of wind gods.

in_hindi.long_meaning: In Hindi, 'Anga' means a limb or a part, but it can also refer to companions or associates of a limb or body part. For example, 'Anga' can be used to refer to the companions of the feet or hands, or it can be used metaphorically to refer to the associates or followers of a particular ideology or group.

in_tamil.name: அங்க
in_tamil.long_meaning: In Tamil, 'Anga' can mean 'limbs' or 'parts' of the body, but it can also refer to 'family' or 'clan'. The word is derived from the root 'angam' which means 'body'. The concept of 'Anga' is deeply rooted in Tamil culture, where family and community are highly valued.

in_telugu.name: అఙ్గ
in_telugu.long_meaning: In Telugu, 'Anga' can mean 'limb' or 'part', but it can also refer to 'tools' or 'instruments'. The word is derived from the root 'angam' which means 'body'. In Hindu mythology, the 'Anga' Maruts are a group of wind gods.
